variants.prompt: A placeholder such as {order_id} must survive. Put the boundaries in order, noting where it is protected.

items.text: Preprocessing replaces it with a typed sentinel before tokenizing.
The model translates around the sentinel.
Validation records the protected span.
Post-checks verify exact restoration of the placeholder.
Release only if restoration succeeded.

variants.hint: Protect before tokenizing; verify after decoding.
variants.explanation: Replace placeholders with typed sentinels, then verify exact restoration.

variants.title: Trace the request
variants.context: One translation request crosses five boundaries: validate language pair, locale, domain, protected spans, and deadline; normalize, segment, tokenize, and preserve markup and placeholders; choose an approved model and decoding policy; check terminology, numbers, entities, placeholders, and quality; then release, abstain, fall back, or send to human review.
variants.prompt: A high-risk legal segment fails a terminology check. Put the boundaries in order, ending with the route.

items.text: The approved model produced candidates.
Validation set the risk tier to high.
Text was prepared with the versioned glossary.
The terminology check failed.
The segment is sent to human review rather than released.

variants.hint: Risk tier determines what happens on failure.
variants.explanation: Human workflow remains the correct route when machine evidence cannot support release.

variants.title: Gate the release
variants.context: Release the target text only when its meaning and protected facts remain attributable to the source. A high model score never overrides a missing number, broken placeholder, unsafe addition, or unsupported pair. Never normalize globally without language-specific evidence.
variants.prompt: A candidate has the best model score but drops a negation. Release it?
options: Yes; the learned metric ranks it above every other candidate.
Yes, with a warning attached for a reviewer to check later.
No. A high model score never overrides a meaning change.
optionFeedback: A learned metric rewards fluency and similarity, and a dropped negation still reads fluently.
Warnings do not fix meaning, and the reversed sentence reaches the reader either way.
Meaning must remain attributable to the source.
variants.hint: What must remain attributable to the source?
variants.explanation: A fluent sentence can still be wrong.

variants.title: Gate the release
variants.context: Release the target text only when its meaning and protected facts remain attributable to the source. A high model score never overrides a missing number, broken placeholder, unsafe addition, or unsupported pair. Never normalize globally without language-specific evidence.
variants.prompt: A cleanup step lowercases and strips accents in every locale to reduce vocabulary. What is the risk?
options: A rule that is harmless in one locale changes meaning in another.
No risk; stripping accents only shrinks the vocabulary table.
Decoding slows down because every segment is rewritten first.
optionFeedback: Never normalize globally without language-specific evidence.
Accents carry meaning in many locales, so a smaller vocabulary is bought with lost distinctions.
Speed is not the issue; the cleanup destroys required surface forms before the model runs.
variants.explanation: Choose and version normalization rules per language.

variants.title: Gate the release
variants.context: Release the target text only when its meaning and protected facts remain attributable to the source. A high model score never overrides a missing number, broken placeholder, unsafe addition, or unsupported pair. Never normalize globally without language-specific evidence.
variants.prompt: A number in the source is 1,000 and the candidate says 100. Which check catches it, and what happens?
options: Nothing; a shifted digit is a minor surface difference.
The model score decides, since it already compares both texts.
The numbers check rejects the candidate regardless of fluency.
optionFeedback: Numbers are protected facts, and 100 instead of 1,000 changes what the reader is told.
Score does not override protected facts, and overlap metrics barely move on one digit.
Protected facts are gates, not weights.
variants.explanation: Reject candidates that break placeholders, numbers, language, or required terms.

variants.title: Size the fleet
variants.context: Worked envelope: 1,500 requests per second × 95 target tokens = 142,500 target tokens per second; at 1,100 tokens per second per replica that is 129.5, so 130 replicas; with 30% headroom, ceil(130 × 1.3) = 169.
variants.prompt: Peak is 1,500 requests per second with 95 generated target tokens each. How many target tokens per second?
variants.hint: Multiply requests by tokens per request.
variants.explanation: 1,500 × 95 = 142,500 target tokens per second; capacity depends on target length, not request count alone.

variants.title: Size the fleet
variants.context: Worked envelope: 1,500 requests per second × 95 target tokens = 142,500 target tokens per second; at 1,100 tokens per second per replica that is 129.5, so 130 replicas; with 30% headroom, ceil(130 × 1.3) = 169.
variants.prompt: 142,500 target tokens per second at 1,100 effective tokens per second per replica. How many replicas, rounded up, before headroom?

mistakes.feedback: Divide by the per-replica rate of 1,100.

variants.title: Size the fleet
variants.context: Worked envelope: 1,500 requests per second × 95 target tokens = 142,500 target tokens per second; at 1,100 tokens per second per replica that is 129.5, so 130 replicas; with 30% headroom, ceil(130 × 1.3) = 169.
variants.prompt: 130 replicas are needed before headroom. With 30% recovery and skew headroom, how many replicas?
variants.explanation: ceil(130 × 1.3) = 169 replicas; these are design assumptions, not benchmark claims.

mistakes.feedback: That is the headroom alone; add it to 130.

variants.title: Decide the release
variants.context: Separate model preference from release constraints: generate a bounded candidate set under a deadline; reject candidates that break placeholders, numbers, language, or required terms; rank the admissible ones with model and quality evidence; return no machine translation when evidence is insufficient.
variants.prompt: Beam search produced several candidates. Put the release decision in order.

items.text: Reject candidates that break placeholders, numbers, language, or required terms.
Generate or retrieve a bounded candidate set under a deadline.
Return no machine translation when the remaining evidence is insufficient.
Rank the admissible candidates with model and quality evidence.

variants.explanation: A higher model score is not equivalent to a releasable translation.

variants.prompt: Every candidate breaks a required term. Put the steps in order, ending with the outcome.

items.text: All candidates fail the terminology rejection.
No machine translation is returned; fallback or human review applies.
Candidates were generated under the deadline.
There is nothing admissible to rank.

variants.hint: An empty admissible set is a legitimate result.
variants.explanation: Return no machine translation when evidence is insufficient.

variants.title: Decide the release
variants.context: Separate model preference from release constraints: generate a bounded candidate set under a deadline; reject candidates that break placeholders, numbers, language, or required terms; rank the admissible ones with model and quality evidence; return no machine translation when evidence is insufficient.
variants.prompt: Beam width is widened to improve quality. Put the release decision in order and note the trade-off.

items.text: Rank the survivors.
Release or abstain; wider search can still prefer a fluent candidate that violates facts.
Reject candidates violating protected facts.
Generate more candidates at higher compute cost within the deadline.

variants.hint: Width is a quality-versus-speed decision, not a correctness guarantee.
variants.explanation: Beam search can recover a better sequence but does not enforce constraints by itself.

variants.title: Choose the route
variants.context: Choose a route, not one universal winner: a specialized pair model for one direction and domain; a dense multilingual model to share parameters; a sparse model with routing concerns; a general-purpose LLM with faithfulness and terminology gates; a human workflow when impact is high.
variants.prompt: One language direction and a regulated domain justify dedicated quality and capacity. Which route?
optionFeedback: Dedicated pairs earn their cost in high-value directions.
A general LLM needs faithfulness gates before release.
variants.hint: Does one direction justify dedicated capacity?
variants.explanation: Choose a model route, not one universal winner.

variants.title: Choose the route
variants.context: Choose a route, not one universal winner: a specialized pair model for one direction and domain; a dense multilingual model to share parameters; a sparse model with routing concerns; a general-purpose LLM with faithfulness and terminology gates; a human workflow when impact is high.
variants.prompt: A general-purpose LLM is proposed for all translation. What must be added before release?
options: A bigger prompt describing the required tone and glossary.
Faithfulness, terminology, latency, and cost gates.
Nothing; the model follows instructions well enough already.
optionFeedback: Prompts are not gates, because nothing checks the output before it reaches the reader.
Flexibility does not replace release evidence.
Instructions do not enforce faithfulness, and a fluent unsupported addition passes unnoticed.
variants.hint: What does the general model lack by default?

variants.prompt: Impact is high and machine evidence cannot support release. Which route?
